entities.name: ORD ord-7bd9bad326d341aaa417f13e30b23965
observations: Directly matched transformation of a heteroaromatic carboxylic acid to the corresponding methyl ester using methanol and thionyl chloride.
The transformation is acid activation followed by methanolysis; no phosphorus incorporation is supported.
Retrieved record did not specify exact temperature, reaction time, base, or workup.

entities.name: Methanol
observations: Serves as the esterifying alcohol and commonly as solvent/nucleophile in the inferred transformation.

entities.name: Thionyl chloride
observations: Most likely activating reagent for converting the carboxylic acid to the methyl ester in methanol.
An external base is generally unnecessary because methanol is used in excess.

entities.name: Methyl ester formation
observations: The observed product is consistent with replacement of a carboxylic-acid hydroxyl group by methoxy, converting –CH2CO2H to –CH2CO2Me.
Cross-coupling, carbonylation, cyclization, and phosphorylation are not supported by the decoded atom changes.
